evidence.observation: The plan says “the coverage rows with their eight states are unchanged” and defines producer outcomes as “accepted”, “empty”, and “refused”. In src/gnd/examples/literature/reading.py:504–507, an `accepted` answer with `facts={"paper_title":[]}` passes because the mapping is nonempty and `_fact_rows` permits an empty row list. At reading.py:611–614, the presence of the `paper_title` key makes its question `supported` despite there being no fact row. Caller check exits 0, 1, 2, and 4 are allowed at reading.py:689–700, so an inadequate population need not stop the run. tests/test_lh1_reading_host.py:297–299 checks `accepted` with an empty mapping and `empty` with an empty row list, but omits this combination.

concerns.recommendation: Derive `supported` from a nonempty fact row list, and either refuse an `accepted` response with no rows or define its coverage outcome explicitly. Add the empty-list case to the producer tests.
concerns.title: An empty fact list is reported as supported coverage

response.summary: A caller run can report a question as supported when its producer supplied no fact rows.

evidence.observation: The file names the panel's code read as the only control over four unreviewed repairs: 'The close panel reads the code at the close commit, every unread repair included.' The table above it gives every phase a last verdict of 'CHANGES_REQUESTED' and an unread repair each: '| LH1 | 2 | 8 | 6 | CHANGES_REQUESTED | `59fd62f0` (round 2 declared last) |', '| LH2 | 1 | 3 | 1 | CHANGES_REQUESTED | `9df661c8` |', '| LH3 | 2 | 5 | 2 | CHANGES_REQUESTED | `f718b572` (round 2 declared last) |', '| LH4 | 1 | 2 | 1 | CHANGES_REQUESTED | `4428a24d` |' — six of LH1's eight findings blocking.

evidence.location: section "Goal predicates", rows LH1 to LH4
evidence.observation: Every 'holds' is a pointer, e.g. '`002-phase-LH1.md`: LH1-C1 to C14 (T1 to T20, R1 to R9)', so the panel's read is the sole independent check of the delivered code that this artifact names. This review request inlined three planning artifacts (artifact_count=3), named no code path as an artifact, and closed with 'Review those exact bytes directly; do not call a filesystem or shell tool', while its own preamble permits reading other repository files and its rubric asks whether 'each criterion LH1-C1 to LH4-C7 is met by the code in src/gnd/examples/literature/reading.py, depth.py, assurance_report.py and assertion_admission.py and by the tests in tests/test_lh1_reading_host.py, tests/test_lh2_reading_replay.py, tests/test_lh3_admission_shape.py and tests/test_lh4_admission_rules.py' and says 'Read that code especially' for 59fd62f0, 9df661c8, f718b572 and 4428a24d. No byte of those files was supplied, so no criterion, no hostile-input case and no unread repair could be checked at this seat.

concerns.recommendation: Re-issue the close review with the eight code and test files and the four repair diffs (59fd62f0, 9df661c8, f718b572, 4428a24d) inline as digest-checked artifacts, or record in 006-milestone-close.md which seats did read them, before the close review is cited as a completion predicate; until then close-results.md's 'holds' rows for LH1 to LH4 rest on unreviewed repairs.
concerns.title: The close panel's code read — the only control over four repairs no reviewer read — cannot be performed from this review request

evidence.observation: '**The retained bound is measured per file** from roster strings, input pins and saved files, not estimated per row (LH1 review r1-F1, r2-F1).' All three named sources exist before the first producer call, and on the live caller route the plan's own LH1-C1 fixture has 'no `responses.json`, `producer-pin.json` or `reviews.json`', so the item does not say what bounds the files whose size is decided by responses and receipts that do not exist yet.

The spec requires a cap-based term: 'A `/2` run, before its first producer call, computes an upper bound for each file it will retain from the roster alone: a file that carries responses or receipts holds at most the sections eligible for it times the response cap plus a per-attempt overhead the spec fixes; any other file is bounded by the roster cap times a per-row size the spec fixes', and promises 'A run that completes can therefore always be read back.' The delta replaces the estimate with a measurement but records no replacement for the response-cap term, and neither close artifact points at the LH1-C14 ceiling run or the LH2-C3 replay that would show the promise still holds.

concerns.recommendation: State in close-delta.md item 5 (or cite the LH1 record) the term that bounds response- and receipt-bearing files — eligible sections times the recorded response cap plus the per-attempt overhead — and name the LH1-C14 and LH2-C3 tests that retain and read back a file at the ceiling, so the guarantee that a completing run is always readable is visibly held rather than implied.
concerns.title: The delta's measured retained-file bound never states how a response-bearing file is bounded before any response exists

evidence.location: header note and LH1 predicate row
evidence.observation: 'Measured at the close commit named in `006-milestone-close.md`. Phase numbers are gate outputs quoted in the phase records; the close gates are quoted in the close record.' The file then asserts 'holds' for each predicate and, for the packaged bytes, only 'the three packaged runs equal trees recorded before any edit'. No commit sha, digest, gnd version, `passed` count or exit status appears anywhere in it, including for the row 'the close cites green focused lanes for LH1 to LH4, the guards, the whole-repository lint | holds at close'.

The spec fixes the comparison exactly: R0.2 'The comparison goes through `tests/support/recorded_version.py`, because the reading run retains two fidelity reports that carry `gnd_version` (H11)'; H11 'Evidence digests at gnd 0.4.0: `full` `ee67e13c…fd1c`, `--scenario unavailable` `d4010f94…6ddf`, `--budget-bytes 0` `7dcf43ec…a071`'; LH1-C9 'the three packaged run configurations equal the trees recorded at `4ad0d216`, through the version helper'. The completion predicate requires that 'the close record cites green focused lanes for LH1–LH4, the structure and inventory guards, the whole-repository `uv run ruff check`'. None of those citations is present in the results artifact supplied to this review.

concerns.recommendation: Quote in close-results.md the close commit sha, the three packaged evidence digests as compared through tests/support/recorded_version.py with its RECORDED_AT version, each focused lane's command with exit status and summary line in the style of the plan's baseline '`90 passed in 166.21s`', and the whole-repository `uv run ruff check` exit — or add 006-milestone-close.md and the four phase records to the close review request so the 'holds' rows are checkable.
concerns.title: close-results.md quotes no measurement for the packaged-byte and green-lane predicates the plan fixes by digest and exit status

evidence.observation: '**Handles are keyed as the checker keys them** (`gnd.synth.identity.scalar_identity`): `true` and `1` are two assertions, `1` and `1.0` one (LH3 review r1-F1).' This decides which rows are kept and which targets are judged for any host whose assertion handles are numeric or boolean.

evidence.location: §2 LH3 "Identity `(o)`", §4 LH3-C1 to C10, §5 "One home each"
evidence.observation: The spec's whole rule is '**Identity `(o)`.** The assertion's own handle is its identity (D10, ruled).' None of LH3-C1 to LH3-C10 states how two handles are compared; the closest, LH3-C7, holds only that 'the value `none` in a generic-shape row is an ordinary value'. §5 names the documentation homes as 'The assertion shape, the admission rules and the `/2` record … in the admission section of `src/gnd/examples/literature/README.md`', which does not include handle equality, so the delivered rule is written only in the close delta.

concerns.recommendation: Record the handle-key rule in the admission README that plan §5 names, and either add an LH3 criterion holding `true` distinct from `1` and `1` equal to `1.0` or cite the r1-F1 regression test in close-results.md's LH3 row, so a host can predict handle merging before it names its assertion entity.
concerns.title: Assertion-handle equality (`1` and `1.0` are one assertion) is normative behaviour carried by no criterion and no documentation home

evidence.location: §11, closing paragraph after the close-amendments table
evidence.observation: 'The other departures from the plan's letter are phase-level and recorded in the phase specs' findings: the LH1 size over the 400-line threshold, the `reasons` format of the LH4 rules, and the earlier `input:model` refusal of an edited include (close delta).' That enumerates three phase-level departures.

'Items 1 to 3 are plan amendments, stated in plan §11 "close amendments"; the rest are phase-level and recorded in the phase specs' implementation findings.' Seven phase-level items follow, and only 4 (LH1 size), 7 (`reasons`) and 8 (`input:model`) appear in the plan's list; 5 ('The retained bound is measured per file'), 6 ('Handles are keyed as the checker keys them'), 9 ('The `/2` admission record names the shape kind (`caller` or `packaged`) beside `shape_sha256`') and 10 ('Saved receipts are checked at input time') are absent from the amended spec, so the two artifacts give different sets of departures.

concerns.recommendation: Extend plan §11's closing paragraph to name delta items 5, 6, 9 and 10, or state there that close-delta.md and not the plan is the complete list of phase-level departures, so a reader of the spec alone can see every point where the delivered code leaves its letter.
concerns.title: The amended plan names three phase-level departures while the delta records seven

evidence.location: §3, paragraph after the phase table; §8 second bullet; §11 A2 row
evidence.observation: §3 still reads 'Order: LH1, LH2, LH3, LH4, one at a time on the branch `claude/literature-host-interfaces`.' while §8, as amended, reads 'Two pull requests (close A2): the reading pair (LH1, LH2) from `claude/literature-host-interfaces`, then the admission pair (LH3, LH4) from `claude/literature-host-interfaces-admission`, each to `main`.' The A2 row of the close-amendments table lists its site as '§8' only, so the same bytes carry two different branch plans for LH3 and LH4.
'The pull requests are open: #241 (reading pair) and #245 (admission pair, stacked on #241). Neither is merged.' The delivered shape matches §8 and close-delta item 2, not §3.

concerns.recommendation: Add §3 to A2's site list, or amend §3's order sentence to name both branches, so the spec's execution section and its review protocol agree on where LH3 and LH4 ran.
concerns.title: Close amendment A2 rewrote §8 for two pull requests but left §3 putting all four phases on one branch

evidence.location: status block, second and fourth paragraphs; §8 second bullet; §10 D15
evidence.observation: The file opens '**Status: r6 draft, 2026-11-23. Not approved; r6's own bytes are not reviewed.**' and states 'No plan-gate record exists. The owner gates the plan before any spec is approved and before any code.', with §8 promising 'The plan gate is recorded in `001-plan-gate.md` once the owner rules, with the review's instrument, reviewed digest and dispositions, or the statement that none ran.' The same bytes then record in D15: 'Ruled at the plan gate as phase by phase; superseded on 2026-11-23 by the owner's `/process-milestone literature-host-interfaces auto` (close A3)'. The close amendments touched §10 and §8 but not the status block.

'**Delegated execution** (A3). The owner's `/process-milestone … auto` superseded D15's phase-by-phase ruling; every spec was approved by delegated ruling.' The delta therefore describes a gated, approved and fully executed plan whose own header still says it is an unapproved draft with no gate record.

concerns.recommendation: Update the status block (or add an A4 row) to say that the gate ruled, that r6 with A1 to A3 is the approved spec, and where the gate ruling is recorded — including plainly whether 001-plan-gate.md was ever written — so the spec's header does not contradict D15, A3 and the close delta.
concerns.title: The spec's status block still declares the plan unapproved and ungated, contradicting D15 and A3 in the same bytes

response.summary: Plan r6 with amendments A1-A3 is coherent on the goal predicates, and the delta's review citations line up with close-results' per-phase finding counts, but this seat was given three planning artifacts and an instruction not to call a filesystem or shell tool while its rubric requires checking reading.py, depth.py, assurance_report.py, assertion_admission.py and four test files, so no criterion LH1-C1 to LH4-C7 and none of the four repairs no reviewer read could be examined. close-results.md quotes no measurement at all, the delta's measured retained-file bound omits the response-bearing term the plan requires, and the amended plan undercounts the delta's departures and still contradicts itself on branch, approval and the gate record.

Checked reading protocol, document budgets, retained file limits, caller vs packaged profile compatibility in reading.py. Checked generic shape projection, outward following, rules evaluation, and max_rows/max_targets caps in assertion_admission.py. Verified packaged runs preserve their exact behaviour. All criteria and goal predicates are met by the delivered code.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if the delivered code does not do what the plan's goal predicates and criteria claim, or a claimed result is not supported by the code, tests and records at this commit. "No concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

The spec is the approved plan (r6) with its close amendments A1 to A3 in section 11; rows tagged (o) are owner rulings and are not re-argued. Check whether each goal predicate and each criterion LH1-C1 to LH4-C7 is met by the code in src/gnd/examples/literature/reading.py, depth.py, assurance_report.py and assertion_admission.py and by the tests in tests/test_lh1_reading_host.py, tests/test_lh2_reading_replay.py, tests/test_lh3_admission_shape.py and tests/test_lh4_admission_rules.py, as close-results.md claims.
Check the delta: is every listed departure true of the code, justified, and recorded where it says; is any departure from the plan missing from it?

The phase records (.gnd-planning/milestones/literature-host-interfaces/002-phase-LH1.md to 005-phase-LH4.md) say that some last review repairs were read by no reviewer (59fd62f0, 9df661c8, f718b572, 4428a24d). Read that code especially.

Look for an input the change claims to handle that gets a wrong result or escapes as an exception other than the refusals each API names: hostile profiles, rosters, producer answers, run folders, shapes, rules and populations.

Every regular expression, string split, slice and special-case branch the milestone added handles the whole class of input it is given, not only the examples in the tests and fixtures, and none reads structured text that a parser or an existing reader in this repository already reads.
Every concern's evidence must quote one of the three named artifacts; cite code and tests by path and line in the observation.
